Judgment
1.
The present reference is u/s 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as L.A. Act).
The land of village Razapur Kalan came under Government acquisition and an Award No.20/03-04 was passed.
The present dispute is pertaining to apportionment of the compensation of land of khasra no.605min (0-10) category A.
The dispute is between aforesaid 2 Interested Persons (hereinafter referred to as IPs).

LAC also remitted an amount of Rs.2,57,015/- being Uoi (Razapur Kalan) vs Kaushalya Devi (2003-04) on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195787728/
1 compensation of aforesaid acquired land.
2. Notice of the present reference u/s 30-31 of L.A. Act was issued to both the IPs.
It is pertinent to mention that LRs of IP-1 & IP-2 have filed their respective claims.
CLAIMS 3. Claim of IP-1 Kaushalya Devi/her LR's :- Yashpal/ LR of IP-1 has filed his claim by way of affidavit.
Yashpal has claimed that his mother was the owner and in possession of the aforesaid acquired land.
In his claim/ affidavit Yashpal has further stated that he has no knowledge whether his mother had sold the said land to the claimant namely Kewal Kumar Suri.
Yashpal has further claimed that LRs of late Smt. Kaushalya Devi are entitled to receive compensation qua said land.
4. Claim of IP No.2/Kewal Kumar Suri:-IP -2/Kewal Kumar Suri has claimed that he had purchased the aforesaid land and was in possession of the same at the time its acquisition by government.
IP-2 has further claimed that he is entitled to receive the entire aforesaid compensation.

Issues:-
5. On completion of pleadings following issues were framed:-

1. Which of the IPs is entitled to the compensation, if so, to what extent ?
2. Relief.
Evidence:-
6. In support of their claim LRs of IP-1 have not led any evidence and they were proceeded exparte vide order dated 14.11.2018.
7. In support of his claim IP-2/ Kewal Kumar Suri has produced/examined two witnesses.
IP-2/W1 is IP-2/ Kewal Kumar Suri himself.
IP-2W1 filed his evidence by way of affidavit i.e. Ex.IP2W1/A and also relied upon documents exhibited as Ex.IP2W1/1 to IP2W1/5.
It is pertinent to mention that IP2W1 was not cross-examined by or on behalf of IP-1 as IP-1 was proceeded exparte vide order dated 14.11.2018.
Testimony of IP2W1has remained unchallenged and unrebutted.
8. IP2W2 is Sh. Balwan Singh.
IP2W2 in his testimony recorded in Court has supported the version/case of IP2 and stated that he had purchased the said land from Smt. Kaushalya Devi (IP-1)and sold the same to IP-2.
IP2W2 also admitted the documents he had executed in favour of IP-2 and further stated that he had handed over possession of said land to IP-2.

It is pertinent to mention that even IP2W2 was not cross-examined by or on behalf of IP-1.
9.
I have heard arguments advanced by Sh. K.K. Kaushik, ld. Counsel for IP-2.
It is pertinent to mention that none had appeared on behalf of IP1 for addressing final arguments.

2

Findings on the issues:-
10.
The claim filed by Lrs of IP-1 is extremely vague one.
In the claim itself LRs of IP-1 have stated that they have no knowledge whether their mother had sold the land to the claimant namely Kewal Kumar Suri.
No evidence has been led by IP-1/her LRs to prove their claim.
LRs of IP-1 have not cross-examined the witnesses produced and examined by IP-2.
It is reiterated that LRs of IP-1 were proceeded exparte vide order dated 14.11.2018.

Thus, the LRs of IP-1 failed to prove their claim and demolish the claim of IP-2.
11.
On the other hand IP-2/Kewal Kumar Suri in his claim has stated that he had purchased the land in question from Balwan Singh and he was in possession of the same at the time of its acquisition.
In support of his claim, IP-2 himself entered into witness box and has proved his claim as well as the documents vide which he had purchased the land in question.
IP2W2 i.e. Balwan Singh in his testimony recorded in Court reiterated the claim of IP2 and stated that he had sold the said land to IP2 and had also given possession thereof to IP2.
12. The testimony of IP2W1 and IP2W2 has remained unchallenged and unrebutted and this Court has no reason to disbelieve the same.

Even otherwise, IP2 has produced and proved the documents vide which IP1/Kaushalya Devi had sold the land in question to Balwan Singh and lateron Balwan Singh had sold the said land to IP2/Kewal Kumar Suri.

13. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, circumstances and discussion made hereinabove I am of the considered view that IP-2/ Kewal Kumar Suri is entitled to receive/get the full/entire compensation amount deposited by LAC in Court.
Both issues are decided accordingly.
14. The reference petition is answered.

15. District Nazir is directed to remit/distribute the awarded amount of the land to IP2/Kewal Kumar Suri in above terms subject to filing of necessary documents, completion of necessary formalities and after receiving the amount from concerned Bank.
16. Copy of this judgment be sent to the LAC.
17. File be consigned to record-room after necessary Digitally compliance.
signed by
DEEPAK DEEPAK DABAS DABAS
